at eje.explanation: "At eje" means "to own": Han ejer to huse (He owns two houses). In everyday talk, Danes often just say at have (to have): Jeg har en bil (I have a car).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **eje** sit eget hus.
sentence.en: He would like to own his own house.

at eksistere.explanation: "At eksistere" means "to exist": Dinosaurer eksisterer ikke længere (Dinosaurs no longer exist). In everyday talk, Danes often say findes (exist) instead: Findes der en bus? (Is there a bus?)

sentence.da: Drager kan ikke **eksistere** i virkeligheden.
sentence.en: Dragons cannot exist in real life.

at eksplodere.explanation: "At eksplodere" means "to explode": Bomben eksploderede (The bomb exploded). It also works for feelings: Han eksploderede af vrede (He exploded with anger).

sentence.da: Flasken kan **eksplodere**, når den bliver for varm.
sentence.en: The bottle can explode when it gets too hot.

at elske.explanation: "At elske" means "to love". It is a strong word, kept mostly for people you truly care about: Jeg elsker dig (I love you). For things and activities, Danes usually say Jeg kan godt lide (I like) or Jeg holder af (I am fond of). Saying you elsker (love) pizza is possible, but it sounds playful.

sentence.da: Hun vil **elske** sine børn for evigt.
sentence.en: She will love her children forever.

at ende.explanation: "At ende" means "to end" and also "to end up": Historien endte godt (The story ended well). Vi endte i Aarhus (We ended up in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, at filmen vil **ende** godt.
sentence.en: I think the movie will end well.

at ende med.explanation: "At ende med" means "to end up with" something, or "to end up doing" something: Jeg endte med en forkølelse (I ended up with a cold). Han endte med at købe en cykel (He ended up buying a bike).

sentence.da: Vi vil nok **ende med** at blive hjemme.
sentence.en: We will probably end up staying at home.

e-boks.explanation: "En e-Boks" means "an e-Boks", the digital mailbox where public offices, banks and companies send you letters.

forms.da: Jeg har et brev i e-Boks.
forms.en: I have a letter in e-Boks.

sentence.da: Jeg har fået et brev i **e-Boks**.
sentence.en: I have received a letter in e-Boks.

eddike.explanation: "Eddike" means "vinegar", the sour liquid used in salad dressing: Tilsæt lidt eddike (Add a little vinegar). It is also one of the ingredients in pickles.

sentence.da: Salaten smager surt, fordi der er **eddike** i.
sentence.en: The salad tastes sour because there is vinegar in it.

effektiv.explanation: "Effektiv" means "efficient" and "effective": Hun er meget effektiv på arbejde (She is very efficient at work). Medicinen er effektiv (The medicine is effective).

sentence.da: Han er meget **effektiv** og bliver hurtigt færdig.
sentence.en: He is very efficient and finishes quickly.

efter.explanation: "Efter" means "after": efter arbejde (after work). In some phrases, it means "for": at lede efter nøglerne (to look for the keys). Before a whole sentence, say efter at: efter at jeg kom hjem (after I came home).

sentence.da: Vi går en tur **efter** middagen.
sentence.en: We go for a walk after dinner.

efter min mening.explanation: "Efter min mening" means "in my opinion" and introduces what you think: Efter min mening er filmen for lang (In my opinion the movie is too long).

sentence.da: **Efter min mening** er suppen for salt.
sentence.en: In my opinion the soup is too salty.

egen.explanation: "Egen" means "own", and it goes with words like min (my) or din (your): mit eget værelse (my own room), mine egne ting (my own things).

sentence.da: Jeg har min **egen** bil.
sentence.en: I have my own car.

egentlig.explanation: "Egentlig" means "actually" or "really", and often hints at a plan that changed: Jeg skulle egentlig arbejde (I was actually supposed to work). In questions it asks what is really true: Hvad vil du egentlig? (What do you really want?).

sentence.da: Jeg ville **egentlig** gå hjem, men jeg blev.
sentence.en: I actually wanted to go home, but I stayed.

egoistisk.explanation: "Egoistisk" means "selfish" and describes someone who thinks only of themselves: Det var egoistisk af ham (That was selfish of him). The opposite is uselvisk (unselfish).

sentence.da: Han er **egoistisk** og tænker kun på sig selv.
sentence.en: He is selfish and only thinks of himself.

ekstra.explanation: "Ekstra" means "extra", more than you already have: en ekstra stol (an extra chair). Before another word, it makes that word stronger: ekstra stor (extra large), ekstra god (extra good).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en **ekstra** stol, tak.
sentence.en: We need an extra chair, please.

ekstremt.explanation: "Ekstremt" means "extremely": Det er ekstremt koldt (It is extremely cold). It is stronger than meget (very).

sentence.da: I dag er det **ekstremt** varmt.
sentence.en: Today it is extremely hot.

elektricitet.explanation: "Elektricitet" means "electricity": Der er ingen elektricitet i hytten (There is no electricity in the cabin). In daily life, Danes often say strøm (power): Strømmen er gået (The power is out).

sentence.da: Vi bruger meget **elektricitet** om vinteren.
sentence.en: We use a lot of electricity in the winter.

elektrisk.explanation: "Elektrisk" means "electric", for things that run on electricity: Min cykel er elektrisk (My bike is electric). For the power itself, Danes say strøm (power): Der er ingen strøm (There is no power).

sentence.da: Min bil er **elektrisk** og kører uden benzin.
sentence.en: My car is electric and runs without gasoline.

elektronik.explanation: "Elektronik" means "electronics", devices like phones and computers. It has no a/an and no plural: Han er glad for elektronik (He likes electronics). For one device, say en enhed (a device).

sentence.da: Butikken sælger **elektronik** som telefoner og computere.
sentence.en: The store sells electronics such as phones and computers.

elendig.explanation: "Elendig" means "miserable" or "terrible": Jeg har det elendigt (I feel terrible). It also describes very poor quality: Han er en elendig sanger (He is a terrible singer).

sentence.da: Den gamle bil er **elendig**, og den starter aldrig.
sentence.en: The old car is terrible, and it never starts.

eller.explanation: "Eller" means "or": te eller kaffe? (tea or coffee?). Added at the end of a question, it asks for agreement, like right?: Du kommer, eller? (You are coming, right?). Don't mix it up with ellers (otherwise): Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent (Hurry up, or we will be late).

sentence.da: Vil du have te **eller** kaffe?
sentence.en: Do you want tea or coffee?

ellers.explanation: "Ellers" means "otherwise" or "or else": Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent (Hurry up, or else we will be late). It also means "else" in questions: Hvad ellers? (What else?). Don't mix it up with eller (or): te eller kaffe (tea or coffee).

forms.da: skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent
forms.en: hurry up, or else we will be late

sentence.da: Skynd dig, **ellers** kommer vi for sent.
sentence.en: Hurry up, or else we will be late.

elleve.explanation: "Elleve" means "eleven": Der er elleve spillere på et fodboldhold (There are eleven players on a football team).

sentence.da: Jeg er **elleve** år gammel.
sentence.en: I am eleven years old.

elvte.explanation: "Elvte" means "eleventh" and gives a place in order, often in dates: Jeg bor på den elvte etage (I live on the eleventh floor). The number itself is elleve (eleven).

sentence.da: Min fødselsdag er den **elvte** maj.
sentence.en: My birthday is May 11th.

en e-mail.explanation: "En e-mail" means "an email". In daily speech, people often shorten it to en mail. You say at sende en e-mail (to send an email) and at modtage en e-mail (to receive an email).

sentence.da: Jeg har sendt dig en **e-mail**.
sentence.en: I have sent you an email.

en edderkop.explanation: "En edderkop" means "a spider": Mange er bange for edderkopper (Many people are afraid of spiders). Der sidder en edderkop i hjørnet (There is a spider in the corner).

sentence.da: Der sidder en stor **edderkop** på væggen.
sentence.en: A big spider is sitting on the wall.

en effekt.explanation: "En effekt" means "an effect", the result of something: Medicinen havde god effekt (The medicine had a good effect). Det har ingen effekt (It has no effect) is a common phrase when something does not work.

sentence.da: Musik har en god **effekt** på mig.
sentence.en: Music has a good effect on me.

en eftermiddag.explanation: "En eftermiddag" means "an afternoon", the part of the day from lunch until evening. Om eftermiddagen means "in the afternoon", and "i eftermiddag" means "this afternoon". The word is built from efter (after) and middag (midday).

sentence.da: Klokken fire er det **eftermiddag**.
sentence.en: It is afternoon at four o'clock.

en efterårsdag.explanation: "En efterårsdag" means "a fall day". It is built from efterår (fall) and dag (day): Vi gik en tur på en blæsende efterårsdag (We went for a walk on a windy fall day).

sentence.da: Det er en kold **efterårsdag** i oktober.
sentence.en: It is a cold fall day in October.

en efterårsferie.explanation: "En efterårsferie" means "a fall break", a week off from school, usually in October: Hvad skal I lave i efterårsferien? (What are you going to do during the fall break?)

sentence.da: Børnene har **efterårsferie** og er hjemme fra skole.
sentence.en: The children have fall break and are home from school.

en ejer.explanation: "En ejer" means "an owner", the person something belongs to. It comes from at eje (to own): Ejeren af restauranten er fra Italien (The owner of the restaurant is from Italy).

sentence.da: Hunden kom hjem til sin **ejer**.
sentence.en: The dog came home to its owner.

en eks.explanation: "En eks" means "an ex", a former boyfriend, girlfriend or partner: Jeg har ikke set min eks i flere år (I have not seen my ex in years). The longer form is en ekskæreste (an ex-boyfriend / ex-girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg så min **eks** i byen, men vi talte ikke.
sentence.en: I saw my ex in town, but we did not talk.

en eksamen.explanation: "En eksamen" means "an exam", the big test at the end of a course: Hun læser til eksamen (She is studying for her exam). It is a formal, graded test, not a quick quiz in class.

sentence.da: Jeg er nervøs, fordi jeg har **eksamen** i morgen.
sentence.en: I am nervous because I have an exam tomorrow.

en ekskæreste.explanation: "En ekskæreste" means "an ex", a former boyfriend or girlfriend: Hun mødte sin ekskæreste i byen (She met her ex in town). It is built from eks- (former) and en kæreste (a boyfriend or girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg er stadig venner med min **ekskæreste**.
sentence.en: I am still friends with my ex.

en eksmand.explanation: "En eksmand" means "an ex-husband": Hendes eksmand bor i Odense (Her ex-husband lives in Odense). It is built from eks- (former) and en mand (a man or husband).

sentence.da: Hendes **eksmand** hentede børnene i går.
sentence.en: Her ex-husband picked up the children yesterday.

en ekspedient.explanation: "En ekspedient" means "a store clerk", the person who helps customers in a store: Ekspedienten hjælper mig (The store clerk helps me). The word is the same for a man or a woman.

sentence.da: Jeg spørger en **ekspedient** om størrelsen.
sentence.en: I ask a store clerk about the size.

en ekspert.explanation: "En ekspert" means "an expert", someone who knows a lot about one subject. After er (is), en is often left out: Hun er ekspert i vin (She is an expert in wine).

sentence.da: Vi skal spørge en **ekspert** om hjælp.
sentence.en: We should ask an expert for help.

en eksplosion.explanation: "En eksplosion" means "an explosion", a sudden loud blast: Der var en eksplosion på fabrikken (There was an explosion at the factory). It can also describe a sudden jump: en eksplosion i priserne (a sudden jump in prices).

sentence.da: Vi hørte en stor **eksplosion** i nat.
sentence.en: We heard a big explosion last night.

en elastik.explanation: "En elastik" means "a rubber band", the stretchy loop that holds things together: Jeg har en elastik om papirerne (I have a rubber band around the papers). It also means the elastic in clothes: Der er elastik i bukserne (There is elastic in the pants).

sentence.da: Jeg samler papirerne med en **elastik**.
sentence.en: I hold the papers together with a rubber band.

en elbil.explanation: "En elbil" means "an electric car". It is built from el (electricity) and bil (car): Min elbil kører 400 kilometer på én opladning (My electric car drives 400 kilometers on one charge).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **elbil**, og den kører uden benzin.
sentence.en: I have an electric car, and it runs without gas.

en elefant.explanation: "En elefant" means "an elephant". Elefanten spiser græs means "The elephant eats grass".

sentence.da: En **elefant** har en lang snabel.
sentence.en: An elephant has a long trunk.

en elektriker.explanation: "En elektriker" means "an electrician", the person you call for wiring and lights: En elektriker sætter lamper op (An electrician puts up lamps).

sentence.da: Vi ringer til en **elektriker**, fordi lyset ikke virker.
sentence.en: We call an electrician because the light does not work.

en elev.explanation: "En elev" means "a pupil", a child or young person who goes to school. It can also mean a trainee or apprentice at a workplace. Adults who study at university are usually called en studerende (a student) rather than elev.

sentence.da: Min søn er **elev** i tredje klasse.
sentence.en: My son is a pupil in third grade.

en elevator.explanation: "En elevator" means "an elevator". Danes also say en lift (a lift). You go up or down med elevatoren (by the elevator).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **elevator** op til femte sal.
sentence.en: We take an elevator up to the fifth floor.

en elkedel.explanation: "En elkedel" means "an electric kettle", used to heat water fast: Elkedlen er tændt (The electric kettle is on). It is built from el (electricity) and kedel (kettle).

sentence.da: Jeg varmer vand til te i min **elkedel**.
sentence.en: I heat water for tea in my electric kettle.

en elpære.explanation: "En elpære" means "a light bulb". It is built from el (electricity) and pære (pear), because the bulb is shaped like one: Elpæren er sprunget (The light bulb has burned out).

sentence.da: Jeg skal købe en ny **elpære** til lampen.
sentence.en: I have to buy a new light bulb for the lamp.

en elregning.explanation: "En elregning" means "an electricity bill". It is el (electricity) plus regning (bill): Jeg betaler min elregning i dag (I am paying my electricity bill today).

sentence.da: Vi får en høj **elregning** i vinter.
sentence.en: We get a high electricity bill this winter.

en emhætte.explanation: "En emhætte" means "a range hood", the fan above a stove that removes steam and smells: Tænd emhætten, når du steger (Turn on the range hood when you fry).

sentence.da: Der er en **emhætte** over komfuret.
sentence.en: There is a range hood over the stove.

en emoji.explanation: "En emoji" means "an emoji", a small picture used in messages. It is the same word as in English: Du kan sende en emoji i stedet for et ord (You can send an emoji instead of a word).

sentence.da: Hun sendte en glad **emoji** til mig.
sentence.en: She sent me a happy emoji.

en ende.explanation: "En ende" means "an end", the last part of something long: i den anden ende af gaden (at the other end of the street). For the end of a story or an event, use en slutning (an ending).

sentence.da: Der er en café i den anden **ende** af gaden.
sentence.en: There is a cafe at the other end of the street.

en endestation.explanation: "En endestation" means "a terminus", the last stop of a train or bus line: Toget kører til endestationen (The train goes to the terminus). It is built from ende (end) and station (station).

sentence.da: Toget har **endestation** i Roskilde.
sentence.en: The train's last stop is Roskilde.

en energikilde.explanation: "En energikilde" means "an energy source". It is built from energi (energy) and kilde (source): Olie og kul er energikilder (Oil and coal are energy sources).

sentence.da: Solen er en ren **energikilde**, og den er gratis.
sentence.en: The sun is a clean energy source, and it is free.

en eng.explanation: "En eng" means "a meadow", an open grassy place where wild flowers grow: Køerne går på engen (The cows are out in the meadow). Do not mix it up with en mark (a field), which is used for crops.

sentence.da: Der vokser vilde blomster på den grønne **eng**.
sentence.en: Wild flowers grow on the green meadow.

en engel.explanation: "En engel" means "an angel", a helper from heaven in stories. It is also used for a very kind person: Du er en engel! (You are an angel!).

sentence.da: Hun malede en **engel** med store vinger.
sentence.en: She painted an angel with big wings.

en englænder.explanation: "En englænder" means "an Englishman" or "an English person": Min lærer er englænder (My teacher is English). The country is England, and the language is engelsk (English).

sentence.da: Han er **englænder**, men han taler godt dansk.
sentence.en: He is English, but he speaks good Danish.

en enke.explanation: "En enke" means "a widow", a woman whose husband has died: Min mormor er enke (My grandmother is a widow).

sentence.da: Hendes mand er død, og nu er hun **enke**.
sentence.en: Her husband has died, and now she is a widow.

en enkeltbillet.explanation: "En enkeltbillet" means "a one-way ticket". It is built from enkelt (single) and billet (ticket). The ticket for the trip back is en returbillet (a return ticket).

sentence.da: En **enkeltbillet** til København, tak.
sentence.en: A one-way ticket to Copenhagen, please.

en entré.explanation: "En entré" means "a hallway", the area just inside the front door: Jeg hænger min jakke i entréen (I hang my jacket in the hallway). Entré also means an admission fee: Der er gratis entré (Admission is free).

sentence.da: Vi tager skoene af i vores **entré**.
sentence.en: We take our shoes off in our hallway.

en episode.explanation: "En episode" means "an episode", one part of a TV show or podcast: Vi ser en episode hver aften (We watch an episode every evening). Et afsnit (an episode) means the same.

sentence.da: Jeg glæder mig til næste **episode** af podcasten.
sentence.en: I am looking forward to the next episode of the podcast.

en erfaring.explanation: "En erfaring" means "experience" you have gained from doing something: Jeg har erfaring med salg (I have experience in sales). For something that happens to you, use en oplevelse (an experience).

sentence.da: Jeg har tre års **erfaring** som kok.
sentence.en: I have three years of experience as a cook.

en etage.explanation: "En etage" means "a floor", as a level of a building: Vi bor på tredje etage (We live on the third floor). The floor you walk on is et gulv (a floor).

sentence.da: Vi bor på tredje **etage** og tager trappen.
sentence.en: We live on the third floor and take the stairs.

en etagebolig.explanation: "En etagebolig" means "an apartment in a multi-story building". It is built from etage (floor) and bolig (home): Vi bor i en etagebolig på tredje sal (We live in an apartment on the third floor).

forms.en: an apartment in a multi-story building
the apartment in a multi-story building

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **etagebolig** midt i byen.
sentence.en: We live in an apartment in the middle of town.

en euro.explanation: "En euro" means "a euro". Hvad koster det i euro? means "What does it cost in euros?".

sentence.da: Billetten til Paris koster tyve **euro**.
sentence.en: The ticket to Paris costs twenty euros.

en europæer.explanation: "En europæer" means "a European", a person from Europe: Vi er alle europæere (We are all Europeans). For things from Europe, use europæisk: europæisk historie (European history).

sentence.da: Som **europæer** kan jeg rejse frit i mange lande.
sentence.en: As a European, I can travel freely in many countries.

end.explanation: "End" means "than": Hun er højere end mig (She is taller than me). It comes after words like større (bigger) or bedre (better). Don't use som for "than". Som means "as": Han er lige så høj som mig (He is as tall as me).

sentence.da: En bil er hurtigere **end** en cykel.
sentence.en: A car is faster than a bicycle.

endda.explanation: "Endda" means "even" and adds something more surprising to what you just said: Han kan endda tale kinesisk (He can even speak Chinese).

sentence.da: Jeg har **endda** mødt kongen.
sentence.en: I have even met the king.

endelig.explanation: "Endelig" means "finally" or "at last": Endelig! (At last!). It also makes an invitation warmer: Tag endelig en kage (Please do take a cake).

forms.en: Be sure not to forget to call.

sentence.da: **Endelig** er det weekend, og vi har fri.
sentence.en: Finally, it is the weekend, and we are off.

endnu.explanation: "Endnu" means "yet" or "still". Ikke endnu means "not yet": Har du spist? Nej, ikke endnu (Have you eaten? No, not yet). With en it means "another": endnu en kop kaffe (another cup of coffee). Before a word like bedre it means "even": endnu bedre (even better).

sentence.da: Jeg er ikke færdig **endnu**.
sentence.en: I am not finished yet.

energi.explanation: "Energi" means "energy", both power that makes things run and the strength you feel: Jeg har ikke energi i dag (I have no energy today). Power from the wall is called strøm (electricity).

sentence.da: Jeg har meget **energi** om morgenen.
sentence.en: I have a lot of energy in the morning.

energisk.explanation: "Energisk" means "energetic" and describes someone full of energy: Han er energisk om morgenen (He is energetic in the morning). The opposite is sløv (sluggish).

sentence.da: Han er **energisk** og løber hver morgen.
sentence.en: He is energetic and runs every morning.

eneste.explanation: "Eneste" means "only" or "single", as in the only one. It normally comes after den, det or de (the): den eneste for en-words, det eneste for et-words. Do not mix it up with kun (just, only): Jeg har kun én bil (I have only one car).

sentence.da: Han er den **eneste** læge her.
sentence.en: He is the only doctor here.

engang.explanation: "Engang" (one word) means "once" or "some day", for a time you do not name exactly: Der var engang... (Once upon a time...), Kom og besøg mig engang (Come and visit me sometime). En gang (two words) means "one time": en gang om dagen (once a day).

forms.en: Come and visit me some day!

sentence.da: Jeg boede i Italien **engang**.
sentence.en: I once lived in Italy.

engelsk.explanation: "Engelsk" means "English", for the language and for things from England. As a school subject, say Jeg har engelsk (I have English, meaning an English lesson). Words for languages start with a small letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Hun er fra England og taler **engelsk**.
sentence.en: She is from England and speaks English.

england.explanation: "England" means "England". It is only one part of the United Kingdom; for Great Britain as a whole, say Storbritannien (Great Britain).

sentence.da: London er en stor by i **England**.
sentence.en: London is a big city in England.

enhver.explanation: "Enhver" means "anyone" or "every", and stresses that it holds for each person: Enhver har ret til en pause (Everyone has the right to a break). With an et-word, it becomes ethvert.

sentence.da: **Enhver** kan lære at svømme.
sentence.en: Anyone can learn to swim.

enig.explanation: "Enig" means "in agreement". Danes say it with er (am/is/are): Jeg er enig (I agree), Det er jeg enig i (I agree with that).

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **enig** med dig om det her.
sentence.en: I completely agree with you about this.

enig med.explanation: "Enig med" means "in agreement with" a person: Jeg er enig med min mor (I agree with my mom). For an idea or opinion, use enig i: Jeg er enig i det (I agree with that).

forms.da: Vi er ikke enige med ham.
forms.en: We do not agree with him.

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **enig med** dig.
sentence.en: I completely agree with you.

enkel.explanation: "Enkel" means "simple" in the sense of plain and not complicated: Opskriften er enkel (The recipe is simple). For easy to do, use let (easy).

sentence.da: Reglen er **enkel**, så alle kan lære den.
sentence.en: The rule is simple, so everyone can learn it.

enkelt.explanation: "Enkelt" means "single" or "simple". En enkelt person (a single person) is just one, and Det er enkelt (It is simple) means it is easy.

sentence.da: Svaret er helt **enkelt**.
sentence.en: The answer is quite simple.

enogtyve.explanation: "Enogtyve" means "twenty-one". Danish says the one first: en-og-tyve is literally one-and-twenty. The same goes for 22, toogtyve (two-and-twenty), and 31, enogtredive (one-and-thirty).

sentence.da: Min søn er **enogtyve** år.
sentence.en: My son is twenty-one years old.

enorm.explanation: "Enorm" means "enormous", far bigger than normal: Hvalen er enorm (The whale is enormous). It also fits big amounts and effects: en enorm succes (a huge success).

sentence.da: Der er en **enorm** hund i vores gade.
sentence.en: There is an enormous dog on our street.

enormt.explanation: "Enormt" means "enormously" and makes the next word much stronger: Det er enormt dyrt (It is enormously expensive). It also fits feelings: Jeg er enormt glad (I am hugely happy).

sentence.da: Den film var **enormt** sjov.
sentence.en: That movie was hugely funny.

ens.explanation: "Ens" means "identical" or "alike" and says that things are the same: De to søstre er ens (The two sisters are alike). You need two or more things to compare.

sentence.da: De to huse er helt **ens**.
sentence.en: The two houses are exactly alike.

ensomhed.explanation: "Ensomhed" means "loneliness", the feeling of being alone even when people are around: Mange ældre kender ensomhed (Many older people know loneliness). Someone who feels it is ensom (lonely): Jeg føler mig ensom (I feel lonely).

sentence.da: Efter flytningen følte hun **ensomhed**, men hun fandt venner.
sentence.en: After the move she felt loneliness, but she found friends.

enten.explanation: "Enten" means "either" and works with eller (or) to give two choices: Vi tager enten bussen eller toget (We take either the bus or the train). Together, enten ... eller means "either ... or".

forms.da: enten i dag eller i morgen

sentence.da: Vi tager **enten** bussen eller toget.
sentence.en: We take either the bus or the train.

enten…eller.explanation: "Enten … eller" means "either … or" and gives two choices: Enten i dag eller i morgen (Either today or tomorrow). Enten goes before the first choice and "eller" before the second. For "neither … nor", say hverken … eller: Jeg vil hverken have kaffe eller te (I want neither coffee nor tea).

forms.da: Enten i dag eller i morgen.
Enten er du med, eller også er du ikke.
forms.en: Either you are in, or you are not.

sentence.da: Vi kan **enten** gå **eller** tage bussen.
sentence.en: We can either walk or take the bus.

er det ...?.explanation: "Er det ...?" means "is it ...?". Danish asks a question by putting er (is) first, with no extra word like do: Er det rigtigt? (Is that right?). Fill the gap with whatever you want to ask about.

sentence.da: **Er det** langt herfra?
sentence.en: Is it far from here?

er du sikker?.explanation: "Er du sikker?" means "are you sure?". Sikker means "sure" or "safe". You can answer Ja, helt sikker (Yes, completely sure). To ask several people, say Er I sikre? (Are you all sure?).

sentence.da: **Er du sikker?** Det er en lang tur.
sentence.en: Are you sure? It is a long trip.

et efternavn.explanation: "Et efternavn" means "a last name", the family name you share with your family. It is made of efter (after) and et navn (a name).

sentence.da: Mit **efternavn** er Hansen.
sentence.en: My last name is Hansen.

et efterår.explanation: "Et efterår" means "an autumn" (or "a fall" in American English), the season between summer and winter. It is made of efter (after) and et år (a year).

sentence.da: Det er **efterår** med mange røde blade.
sentence.en: It is fall, with many red leaves.

et egern.explanation: "Et egern" means "a squirrel": Der løber et egern i parken (A squirrel is running in the park). It has a long bushy tail: Et egern har en busket hale (A squirrel has a bushy tail).

sentence.da: Et **egern** klatrer op i det høje træ.
sentence.en: A squirrel climbs up the tall tree.

et ekko.explanation: "Et ekko" means "an echo", a sound that comes back: Der er ekko i kirken (There is an echo in the church).

sentence.da: I bjergene kan man høre et **ekko**.
sentence.en: In the mountains you can hear an echo.

et eksempel.explanation: "Et eksempel" means "an example": Her er et eksempel (Here is an example). For example is til eksempel, short t.eks., or for eksempel, short f.eks.

sentence.da: Kan du give et **eksempel**?
sentence.en: Can you give an example?

et eksperiment.explanation: "Et eksperiment" means "an experiment", a test to find something out: Vi laver et eksperiment i timen (We do an experiment in class). The matching verb is at eksperimentere (to experiment).

sentence.da: Børnene laver et **eksperiment** med vand.
sentence.en: The children do an experiment with water.

et emne.explanation: "Et emne" means "a subject" or "a topic" to talk or write about: Emnet i dag er sundhed (Today's topic is health). For math or history at school, use et fag instead.

sentence.da: Hvilket **emne** skal vi tale om?
sentence.en: Which topic should we talk about?

et enkeltværelse.explanation: "Et enkeltværelse" means "a single room", a hotel room for one person. It is made of enkelt (single) and et værelse (a room).

sentence.da: Jeg rejser alene og vil have et **enkeltværelse**.
sentence.en: I travel alone and want a single room.

et escape room.explanation: "Et escape room" means "an escape room", a game where a group is locked in a room and solves puzzles to get out: Vi var i et escape room (We were in an escape room). Danes use the English words.

sentence.da: Vi løste alle opgaverne i vores **escape room** og kom ud.
sentence.en: We solved all the tasks in our escape room and got out.

et eventyr.explanation: "Et eventyr" means both "a fairy tale" and "an adventure": Askepot er et eventyr (Cinderella is a fairy tale). Rejsen var et eventyr (The trip was an adventure).

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **eventyr** for børnene hver aften.
sentence.en: I read a fairy tale to the children every evening.

eu.explanation: "EU" means "the EU", the group of European countries that work together. Say i EU (in the EU): Danmark er med i EU (Denmark is a member of the EU).

sentence.da: Vi må arbejde i alle lande i **EU**.
sentence.en: We may work in all the countries in the EU.

europa.explanation: "Europa" means "Europe": Jeg bor i Europa (I live in Europe).

sentence.da: Danmark ligger i **Europa**.
sentence.en: Denmark is in Europe.

europæisk.explanation: "Europæisk" means "European", for things that belong to Europe: europæisk mad means "European food" and "europæisk musik" means "European music".

sentence.da: Danmark er et **europæisk** land.
sentence.en: Denmark is a European country.

evig.explanation: "Evig" means "eternal", lasting forever: evig fred (eternal peace). It also fits things that never seem to end: en evig diskussion (an endless discussion).

sentence.da: De lovede hinanden **evig** kærlighed ved brylluppet.
sentence.en: They promised each other eternal love at the wedding.

evigt.explanation: "Evigt" means "forever": Din hjælp husker jeg evigt (I will remember your help forever). It is also used in a joking way for a very long wait.

sentence.da: Det varer **evigt**, når man venter på bussen.
sentence.en: It lasts forever when you wait for the bus.
